text:
Happy Tuesday! We're starting off cold and gray, right around freezing, but don't let the early look fool you. High pressure is parked just to our southwest, and that's going to keep us quiet and dry for days. The clouds should give way to a mostly sunny afternoon with a high near 53, a good 10 degrees above normal for mid-November. It's a light-breeze kind of day, so the only thing you'll want is a jacket for the morning. The sun sets a little after 4:20, so get your walk or ride in earlier rather than later.

Tonight turns mostly cloudy and a lot milder, with a low around 39, so tomorrow morning won't be nearly as frosty. Wednesday is partly sunny with a high near 56. The forecasters and the models all agree on that, though one of the TV outlets leans a few degrees warmer, so a spot or two could flirt with 60. The mild, dry run continues through Saturday, and showers hold off until late Sunday. No umbrella needed for now. Just enjoy it.

  1. Dry weather continues with a warming trend expected through the end of this week.

AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 123 AM EST Tuesday... No significant changes were made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Low level moisture trapped beneath an inversion has led to low clouds over the Adirondacks overnight. We also have some fog forming in the valleys where the skies have cleared as surface high pressure is in control of our weather with light winds. Center of surface high pressure will remain nearly stationary to the southwest of our region, but this will provide us with very quiet weather through this week. Temperatures will be about 10 degrees above seasonal normals during the day, and about 5 degrees above normal at night. Each day we should have partly to mostly sunny skies, with mainly clear nights as well. KEY MESSAGE 2: Our nice clear and dry stretch will hold on for one more day this weekend on Saturday before shower chances return for Sunday into Monday. Temperatures Saturday will be similar to that of the work week with highs in the mid to upper 50s and generally clear skies as a secondary ridge, associated with our overarching high passes through. The high centered over the Mid-Atlantic will slide east, but models remain uncertain as to how much the high departs, in addition to how much it weakens. This will play a role for our shower chances Sunday into Monday. There is strong model agreement that a coastal low will develop off the Carolina coast Sunday. However, models begin to diverge on the track of the system towards next week. The GFS and notably the Google AI Deepmind phase this system with an approaching Great Lakes shortwave late Sunday bringing widespread shower chances from south to north; the steadiest of which is focused over southern Vermont. This track depicts the departing high as keeping its strength off the east coast, amplifying the Great Lakes shortwave, and dragging the coastal low north into our region. Conversely, the ECMWF and CMC weaken the departing high, keeping our pattern more progressive, and tracking the coastal low out to see, more near Benchmark. This leaves us with a weaker Great Lakes shortwave, which favors lighter showers mainly across the Adirondacks and areas near the International Border. Currently consensus favors the latter of the two solutions, but we will closely monitor trends for the weekend into next week. Regardless, our temperatures will return to seasonable levels to start off next week with highs back into the 40s.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Tuesday! For the most part, any clouds from Monday have now cleared, which means we started the day cooler with most places in the 20s and lower 30s. Clear skies and sunshine will continue through the day, warming us back up into the upper 40s and low to mid 50s by this afternoon. Tonight will be a bit warmer, with overnight lows settling into the mid to upper 30s by early Wednesday morning. Through Wednesday there may be a few more clouds mixing in from time to time, but with that being said, still plenty of sunshine as temperatures climb toward the mid and upper 50s, with some spots approaching 60. It’s a very similar story for Thursday with partly cloudy skies overhead, and temperatures again in the mid and upper 50s if not close to 60. Friday looks like it will be the warmest day of the week, as mostly sunny skies overhead will help drive our temperatures toward the upper 50s and low to mid 60s, possibly for some spots to the south. We head into the weekend on a nice note for Saturday with mostly sunny skies overhead and temperatures again heading toward the upper 50s and low to mid 60s. Just a degree or so cooler than Friday. Sunday again looks a degree or two cooler than Saturday. We start Sunday dry, but we could find the chance of a few showers by later Sunday evening and night. A few showers may linger into early Monday, but we are dry by later in the day. Temperatures are cooler Monday, back in the 40s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-16T23:55:00Z — same caveat): Brighter and milder Tuesday, as highs soar into the 50s — High pressure continues to build in tonight, so the sky turns mostly clear. It will be seasonably cold, with lows in the 20s to around 30. Tuesday marks the transition toward brighter and warmer weather. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with highs reaching the low to mid-50s. The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with plenty of sunshine and highs in the upper 50s to low 60s! The nice stretch continues this weekend, as it stays mostly dry and mild. Expect nearly full sunshine Saturday. A south breeze picks up on Sunday, as a cold front approaches. A few late-day showers are likely. Highs will be near 60 both days. Behind the front, more seasonable air returns early Thanksgiving week. Highs fall back to the 30s and low 40s. A few showers are possible around the holiday, as it turns a bit milder.
